## Assistant (build · glm-5.3-flash · 42.8s)

_Thinking:_

Now I have a very complete picture of the firmware's motion engine. Critical findings:

**The motion engine is NOT GRBL's planner-driven stepping anymore.** It's a Bresenham tracer (stepper_info) driven by a 1ms software timer, moving ONE axis at a time (motor_current points at the single motor being driven), batching 8 encoder counts per `hal_motor_step` call. This explains:
- "reduce vibrations when X and Y axes are driven together" issue in README — X and Y never truly move simultaneously; the Bresenham alternates axes in 8-step bursts (actually 1 "step" = 8 encoder counts each call). Diagonal moves are choppy.
- Feedrate control is per-axis step interval computed at block load (step_dtx = 60000/(rate*steps_per_mm)), no acceleration profile AT ALL (st_update_plan_block_parameters is #if 0'd, prep code mostly gutted). Actually let me check if there's acceleration... The planner computes the trapezoid but st_prep_buffer just takes pl_block->programmed_rate. So no accel → jerky starts/stops, stalls on hard moves.
- Stall detection: In st_execute_next_step — if motor still DRIVEN after timer expires (step not completed by encoder), wd_stall_counter++ until hard_limit_threshold (200!) → then treat as hard limit. Plus the encoder-side watchdog in hal_motor_stall_detection (called from watchdog.c every 1ms).

So "homing" works by: drive into hard stop → encoder stops counting → watchdog (200ms×?) → limits_set_state → GRBL homing logic sees "limit switch" triggered. Crude.

- Top panel: buttons (POWER, PAUSE, UPDOWN, LOGO), LEDs; RN4678 BT module on UART (unused)
- Debug: PICkit header (MCLR/PGD/PGC) — bootloader cutcutgo-bl installed
- Power: barrel jack 12V(?) with regulators; POWER_TRIGGER MOSFET for soft power off

**3. Community RE landscape**
- virtualabs/cutcutgo + docs + leHACK 2023 talk + schematics PDF + reverse PCB SVG (85MB, download available)
- Hackaday project 187535 "Cricut Hacking" (Explore/Air, similar DC-servo+H-bridge architecture)

- Alternative path: RFCOMM BLE protocol RE (issue #28 comment — python control of Explore 3; original protocol exists but vendor-locked Design Space)

**4. Viability & gaps for user's goals**
- Homing improvement: feasible. Current: stall detection at 1ms with threshold 200 (way too slow for homing: 200 iterations × 1ms timer... actually st_execute_next_step wd_stall_counter++ per timer expiry, > hard_limit_threshold (200)). Improvements: per-phase thresholds (seek: fast detect ~20-30ms; locate: fine), multi-stage seek/locate/pull-off already in GRBL limits logic; add Y homing; back-off after stall; encoder error-based stop
- Stall control: fix wd_armed-from-zero bug (blocked-at-start never detects); commanded-vs-actual step error (lead/lag); direction-change flush; per-axis thresholds; report feed-hold instead of full alarm on mid-job stall
- Blade detection: I2C EEPROM read (24LC/24AA type) on tool insertion; need I2C PLIB enable + protocol; J500 pins 1/2 (SDA/SCL). Plus rotation-encoder gating: no encoder pulses while driving → no tool/no blade seated. Also head presence via POWER_STATE_OUT?
- Pressure detection: no current feedback (A4950 LSS not routed to ADC — confirm on reverse SVG). - Z homing: TOOL lift → hard stop top; currently Z homes whichever TOOL motor = stepper_info.tool (selected_tool). Need homing per-clamp with tool present, plus depth calibration (blade offsets).
- Calibration: steps/mm mapping currently coupled to 8-count batches (DEFAULT_X 11.76 ⇒ 94.08 counts/mm vs theory 100). Recalibrate properly; persist via flash-emulated EEPROM (must implement eeprom.c on PIC32 flash rows; guard during motion).
- Usability: fix position reporting (sync sys_position with encoder), implement eeprom, soft power via POWER_TRIGGER, buttons as feed-hold/cycle-start, BLE GATT serial via RN4678 (optional), Inkscape/inkcut-cutcutgo host already exists.

- No current feedback; DC motor closed-loop quality; 1ms timer resolution limits feedrate accuracy (max ~60000/(rate·steps/mm) integer ms); X+Y diagonal quality needs true coordinated motion or at least PID velocity control; PIC32MX 96MHz single core handles CN interrupts at high encoder rates (compute: 100 counts/mm at 3000mm/min = 50mm/s → 5kHz encoder events per axis — fine).

MAX=800 (33%), MIN=2300 (96%) — so SPEED_MAX/MIN names are backwards in meaning of magnitude: they intended "max speed = 800 ticks"? For a DC motor at fixed P supply, duty ∝ speed; HAL_MOTOR_SPEED_X=2000 ≈ 83% duty. And "kick" 100 (4%) for start. OK.)

Also note X homing in HOMING_CYCLE_1 with only X — Y missing. And in limits_go_home the Z homing via TOOL motors: which motor gets homed depends on stepper_info.tool selected_tool.

Also the halt/limit semantics: hitting a stall during a job triggers mc_reset + EXEC_ALARM_HARD_LIMIT → full abort (host must $X). Better: feed hold + retract.

# Investigación: CutCutGo / Cricut Maker 1 (Champagne)

## 1. Qué es este código

Fork del proyecto **cutcutgo de virtualabs (Damien Cauquil)**: un puerto de **GRBL 1.1** al PIC32MX470F512L de la placa original de la Cricut Maker, con bootloader custom (`cutcutgo-bl`) ya instalado en tu máquina. Ya corta/traza en GCODE con ambas pinzas A/B. Docs: `virtualabs.github.io/cutcutgo` (incluye **esquemáticos invertidos en PDF** y el PCB completo en SVG — ya los descargué a `/tmp/opencode/ccg/`).

## 2. Barrido de hardware (confirmado)

| Bloque | Detalle |
|---|---|
| **MCU** | PIC32MX470F512L, 96 MHz (`SYS_FREQ`), 512KB flash / 128KB RAM. Port de debug/PGC/PGD accesible |
| **Motores** | 5 canales DC con encoder cuadratura óptico (gearmotors Johnson tipo HC385MG): **X** (correa cabezal, ~0.01mm/count), **Y** (rodillos que mueven la cama), **TOOL1**, **TOOL2** (mecanismo de pinza A y B del cabezal), **ACCESSORY** (3er canal del cabezal) |
| **Drivers** | 3× **A4950E** (U1=Y, U2=X, U3=head) + 1× **A4954** dual (U4: TOOL1/TOOL2), PWM 20 kHz (Timer2/OCx), modo slow-decay |
| **Cabezal (ribbon J500, 34 pines)** | **Bus I²C (SDA=RA3, SCL=RA2) → EEPROM de identificación de herramienta** (¡detección de herramienta por hardware, hoy sin usar!), 3 pares de encoders adicionales (rotación pinza A, rotación pinza B, **engranaje de profundidad de pinza B** = posición Z real de la herramienta), `POWER_STATE_OUT` |
| **Interfaz** | USB CDC (ACM), módulo **RN4678 BR/EDR+LE en UART sin usar** (hay ruta para BLE), botones POWER/PAUSE/UP/LOGO, LEDs, MOSFET `POWER_TRIGGER` para apagado software |
| **Límites** | **No hay endstops**. Homing original = embestir el tope mecánico y detectar por pérdida de pulsos del encoder (stall). `limits.c` emula switches con `g_hard_limits` |

**Dato clave para "presión":** el A4950 limita corriente por chopping (LSS con shunt 0.24Ω + VREF) pero **esa señal no llega a ningún ADC del MCU** → no hay feedback de corriente. La fuerza solo puede estimarse por encoder (lag/missing counts) y PWM vs. velocidad real (proxy de back-EMF), o con un mod de hardware (LSS → pin ADC libre).

## 3. Estado real del firmware (lo que encontré)

1. **Motor de movimiento reescrito**: Bresenham sobre un timer software de 1ms que mueve **un motor a la vez** en ráfagas de 8 counts de encoder (`st_execute_next_step`, stepper.c:566). **No hay perfil de aceleración** (el planner trapezoidal se ignora) → explica el issue #22 (ruido en diagonales X+Y) y #17 (círculos ovalados).
2. **Stall detection débil** (motor.c:911 + stepper.c:570): watchdog de 1ms contra threshold fijo 200 (~200ms a full duty). Bug: si el motor está bloqueado **desde el paso 0**, `wd_armed` nunca se arma → nunca detecta stall (el motor se queda energizado).
3. **Homing**: `HOMING_CYCLE_0=Z, CYCLE_1=X` → **Y jamás se homing**. Stall = "limit switch" con threshold único para homing y para trabajo. `HOMING_FORCE_SET_ORIGIN` activo.
4. **eeprom.c 100% stub** (devuelve 0, no escribe) → **la configuración `$` no persiste entre arranques**; la calibración sería inútil sin arreglar esto (emulación en flash del PIC32).
5. **Reportes de posición rotos** (issue #20): `sys_position` no se sincroniza con los counts del encoder en este port.
6. **Sin usar hoy**: I²C del cabezal (detección de herramienta), encoders de rotación/engranaje del cabezal, RN4678 BLE, `POWER_TRIGGER`, spindle/coolant stubs.
7. Comunidad: variantes de placa ATH-84-110-X2 (la "estándar") vs ATH-84-114-X1 (compatibilidad dudosa, issues #27/#30). Ruta alternativa sin flashear: protocolo original por RFCOMM/BLE (issue #28).

## 4. Viabilidad de tus objetivos

| Objetivo | Viabilidad | Ruta |
|---|---|---|
| Homing mejorado | **Alta** | Thresholds por fase (seek rápido/locate lento), añadir homing de Y, pull-off real, back-off tras stall, 2-3 ciclos de locate (ya soportado por GRBL) |
| Control de stalling | **Alta** | Arreglar bug `wd_armed`, comparar comandado vs. real (error de seguimiento), thresholds por eje/fase, en trabajo → feed-hold en vez de alarm+reset |
| Detección de hoja/herramienta | **Alta (por hardware existe)** | Leer EEPROM I²C del cabezal (J500 pines 1-2) + gating por encoder de rotación: sin pulsos al accionar = sin herramienta. Falta driver I²C (PIC32MX lo trae) |
| Detección de presión | **Media** | Sin feedback de corriente. Opciones: estimador de carga por lag encoder + PWM/speed; stall graduado del motor de Z al presionar; o mod (LSS→ADC) |
| Homing de Z | **Alta** | Motor de elevación → tope mecánico superior, calibrar offset por pinza; homing separado por clamp |
| Calibración | **Alta** | `DEFAULT_*_STEPS_PER_MM` hoy = counts/mm ÷ 8 (acoplado a las ráfagas); recalibrar y **persistir** (exige implementar eeprom en flash) |
| Uso útil | **Alta** | Fix de reportes + eeprom + homing completo ya la hace usable con senders GRBL estándar (o inkcut-cutcutgo que ya existe) |

**Conclusión: el proyecto es viable y el trabajo pesado (RE + puerto GRBL) está hecho.** Los huecos son de ingeniería de firmware bien acotados.

## 5. Orden que recomiendo

1. **eeprom en flash** (todo lo demás depende de persistir calibración)
2. **Stall/homing robusto** (bug wd_armed, thresholds por fase, homing de Y y Z por pinza)
3. **Sincronizar `sys_position` con encoders** (reportes y soft-limits correctos)
4. **I²C del cabezal** → detección de herramienta/hoja
5. Estimador de presión + calibración de fuerza
6. Accesorios: `POWER_TRIGGER`, botones como hold/cycle-start, BLE por RN4678

¿Quieres que empiece por alguno (sugeriría el #1+#2 juntos), o prefieres que primero valide los puntos abiertos del hardware sobre la máquina real (mapeo exacto encoders J500↔RG, POWER_STATE_OUT, lectura I²C de la EEPROM de una herramienta)?

# Espacio y viabilidad de grblHAL

## 1. Memoria del PIC32MX470F512L (según los linker scripts del repo)

| Región | Standalone | Con bootloader cutcutgo-bl |
|---|---|---|
| **Flash programa** | 512 KB (`0x9D000000`, `0x80000`) | Bootloader ocupa los primeros 72 KB → app en `0x9D012000` con **448 KB libres** (`0x6E000`) |
| **RAM** | 128 KB (`0x20000`) | **128 KB completos** |
| Boot flash separada | 12 KB | Ya usada por el reset handler |

El firmware actual (GRBL + Harmony USB + buffers) ronda típicamente 100–200 KB → **te sobran ~250–350 KB de flash**. ## 2. ¿grblHAL? Posible, pero no es un flash-and-go

**Espacio: sí, sin problema.** El core de grblHAL son ~50–100 KB flash y pocos KB de RAM.

**El problema no es espacio, es que no hay driver:**
- grblHAL es core C99 + **driver de hardware obligatorio**; existen >15 drivers oficiales, todos ARM (STM32, RP2040, ESP32, Teensy 4.x, Due/SAM3X, MSP432, LPC…). **No existe driver PIC32MX** (MIPS). Habría que escribirlo entero: USB CDC, timers del stepper ISR, GPIO, I²C, NVM/settings, PWM.
- Más grave: grblHAL genera **pulsos step/dir para steppers**. Esta máquina son **DC con encoder en lazo cerrado** — ni GRBL ni grblHAL tienen ese modelo de motor. La pieza valiosa de cutcutgo (HAL de motores + Bresenham DC + stall detection) tendría que reimplementarse dentro de grblHAL como driver/plugin custom.

**Traducción:** portar grblHAL = rehacer desde cero la integración que cutcutgo ya tiene funcionando, para ganar su ecosistema (ioSender, plugins, settings extendidos, eventos). Es viable pero son semanas de trabajo y riesgo.

**Mi recomendación:** quedarse con la base cutcutgo y *cherry-pick* lo bueno de grblHAL (abstracción de settings en flash, arquitectura de eventos/plugins, más parámetros `$`). Eso encaja con tu plan de homing/stall/detección sin tirar nada.

**CPU budget PIC32MX470 @ 96MHz (MIPS M4K, ~1.5 DMIPS/MHz ≈ 144 DMIPS):**

**Algorithms to implement (rewrite of hal/motor + stepper integration):**
1. Per-motor **cascaded control**: position PID (or P+velocity-PI with back-EMF feedforward) at 1 kHz, PWM output.
2. **Coordinated motion**: keep GRBL planner; segment buffer outputs per-tick position increments for ALL axes simultaneously (replace single-motor Bresenham); each axis has independent loop → true diagonal moves, no grinding.
3. **Trapezoidal + S-curve (jerk-limited) profiles** restored from GRBL planner (it's already there, just bypassed).
4. **Stall/fault**: observer = position error window vs speed + kick-start logic; adaptive thresholds; block-at-start detection (fix wd_armed bug); stall during job → controlled stop + feed-hold, during homing → limit trigger.
5. **Homing state machine**: seek (fast) → locate (slow, 3 cycles) → pull-off with hysteresis; repeatability measurement (N-cycle std-dev) at calibration; store homing offsets per axis/tool.
6. **Calibration (robust, min deviation)**:

   - goal "mínimo desvio": homing repeatability target ≤ 1 count (X 0.01mm) — with locate cycles and low speed + mechanical deceleration profile.

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:22.04
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential wget ca-certificates unzip python3 file libc6-i386 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ARG XC32_VERSION=4.20
ARG XC32_URL=https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/softwarebedposables/xc32-v4.20-full-install-linux-installer.run
ARG DFP_URL=https://packs.download.microchip.com/Microchip.PIC32MX_DFP.1.5.259.atpack

RUN wget -q "${XC32_URL}" -O /tmp/xc32.run && chmod +x /tmp/xc32.run && \
    /tmp/xc32.run --mode unattended --prefix /opt/microchip/xc32/v${XC32_VERSION} && \
    rm /tmp/xc32.run
ENV PATH="/opt/microchip/xc32/v${XC32_VERSION}/bin:${PATH}"

RUN mkdir -p /opt/packs/Microchip && \
    wget -q "${DFP_URL}" -O /tmp/dfp.zip && \
    mkdir -p /opt/packs/Microchip/PIC32MX_DFP/1.5.259 && \
    unzip -q /tmp/dfp.zip -d /opt/packs/Microchip/PIC32MX_DFP/1.5.259 && rm /tmp/dfp.zip
ENV DFP_DIR=/opt/packs/Microchip/PIC32MX_DFP/1.5.259

WORKDIR /work
```

**Default flow:** Research (if needed) → Plan → Verify → Done

**Research-only mode (`--research-phase <N>`):** Spawn `gsd-phase-researcher` for phase `N`, write `RESEARCH.md`, then exit before the planner runs. Useful for cross-phase research, doc review before committing to a planning approach, and correction-without-replanning loops where iterating on research alone is dramatically cheaper than re-spawning the planner. Replaces the deleted research-phase command (#3042).

**Research-only modifiers:**
- **No flag** — when `RESEARCH.md` already exists, auto-uses it: emits a one-line notice and exits cleanly, no prompt.
- **`--research`** — force-refresh: re-spawn the researcher unconditionally, no prompt. Bypasses the existing-RESEARCH.md auto-use path.
- **`--view`** — view-only: print existing `RESEARCH.md` to stdout. Does not spawn the researcher. Cheapest mode for the correction-without-replanning loop. If no `RESEARCH.md` exists yet, errors with a hint to drop `--view`.

**Orchestrator role:** Parse arguments, validate phase, research domain (unless skipped), spawn gsd-planner, verify with gsd-plan-checker, iterate until pass or max iterations, present results.
</objective>

Phase number: 1 (optional — when omitted, the orchestrating workflow reads ROADMAP.md and selects the next unplanned phase; `gsd-tools.cjs` itself has no auto-detect feature and requires an explicit phase number)

**Flags:**
- `--research` — Force re-research even if RESEARCH.md exists
- `--skip-research` — Skip research, go straight to planning
- `--gaps` — Gap closure mode (reads VERIFICATION.md, skips research)
- `--skip-verify` — Skip verification loop
- `--prd <file>` — Use a PRD/acceptance criteria file instead of discuss-phase. Parses requirements into CONTEXT.md automatically. Skips discuss-phase entirely.
- `--ingest <path-or-glob>` — Use one or more ADR files instead of discuss-phase. Parses locked decisions + scope fences into CONTEXT.md automatically. Skips discuss-phase entirely.
- `--ingest-format <auto|nygard|madr|narrative>` — Optional ADR parser format override (`auto` default).
- `--reviews` — Replan incorporating cross-AI review feedback from REVIEWS.md (produced by `/gsd-review`)
- `--text` — Use plain-text numbered lists instead of TUI menus (required for `/rc` remote sessions)
- `--mvp` — MVP enrichment on top of the default tracer-first ordering: frames the phase goal as a user story and, on Phase 1 of a new project, also emits `SKELETON.md` (Walking Skeleton). Vertical slicing itself is now the default (see `--no-tracer`); `--mvp` no longer *turns it on*. Can be persisted on a phase via `**Mode:** mvp` in ROADMAP.md.
- `--no-tracer` — Opt out of the default **tracer-first** decomposition and plan horizontal layers (the legacy default). By default every plan LEADS with one production-quality end-to-end `tracer` slice that is verified before any expansion task.
- `--no-reversibility-gates` — Suppress the human checkpoint that a **one-way-door** decision normally earns, for runs you intend to leave unattended. By default a decision rated `one-way` (undo needs a migration, breaks a published contract, or is impossible) gets a `checkpoint:decision` before the task implementing it. Ratings are still recorded on tasks and `costly` items still flagged — the flag changes what stops the run, not what the plan remembers.

Normalize phase input in step 2 before any directory lookups.

2. A clarification question: "el bootloader había que rehacerlo? lo digo porque realmente ya está instalado, solo debería controlar la instalación del soft no?" — Did the bootloader need to be redone? It's already installed; it should just control software installation, right?

Answer: No, the bootloader was NOT redone. The bootloader (cutcutgo-bl) is already installed on the machine and stays untouched. What happened in research/planning is that the bootloader's SOURCE CODE was used as a *reference* (it contains the verified NVM/flash write sequence — plib_nvm.c — that runs on this exact machine), and the researcher also verified a key property: the bootloader only erases flash pages covered by UF2 blocks in the app region (0x1D010000–0x1D080000), so a reserved NVM page at 0x1D07F000 survives reflashing. The firmware we're building *vendors* (copies) that flash-write sequence into its own module (nvm_flash.c) because the application needs to write settings to flash itself — a capability the bootloader has but the app firmware currently lacks (eeprom.c is a stub).

Why did it take long? Honest accounting:
- This was the **setup phase**: GSD project initialization (PROJECT.md, REQUIREMENTS, ROADMAP with 7 phases/milestones division) + full planning cycle for Phase 1 (research agent + pattern mapper + planner + plan-checker with a revision loop) — those are one-time costs that make the following phases faster.
- Subagent spawns had some network failures/retries (one roadmapper retry).
- The first executor run was aborted mid-task and had to be re-dispatched with resume verification.
- Builds in Docker take ~1-2 min each and the tracer ran several of them.
- Actual code delivered in the execution so far: tracer with nvm.c real + fake_flash + Unity test green + tools/ committed + BUILD-01 verified. Only 1 of 5 plans executed so far.

Also note: the long part was mostly orchestration overhead (agents, verification loops), not the machine or the build. Now that plans exist and the simulator scaffold exists, next waves go faster.

## Por qué tardó

## El bootloader: NO se rehace ✓

Tienes razón exacta: **el bootloader ya instalado no se toca** — sigue haciendo su trabajo (flasheo por USB/UF2 manteniendo PAUSE).

Lo que pasó es que su **código fuente se usó como referencia**, por dos razones:

1. **El bootloader contiene la secuencia de escritura flash verificada** (`plib_nvm.c`: NVMCON/NVMKEY, page erase, row write) que **ya corre en tu máquina**. La app necesita esa misma secuencia para guardar settings en flash (hoy `eeprom.c` es un stub que no persiste nada). La **copiamos** (vendorizar) dentro de `nvm_flash.c` del firmware — no reemplazamos el bootloader.

2. **Verificamos una propiedad crítica**: al reflashear por USB, el bootloader solo borra las páginas del rango de la app (`0x1D010000–0x1D080000`). Por eso reservamos la página de settings en `0x1D07F000` — **tus settings/calibración sobrevivirán a las actualizaciones de firmware**. Eso era precisamente una de las preguntas abiertas del research.

## Objective
- Evolving cutcutgo firmware (GRBL 1.1 port for Cricut Maker 1 Champagne, PIC32MX470F512L) toward a reliable, self-calibrating CNC machine with robust homing, stall detection, tool detection, pressure estimation, and minimal deviation calibration
- Currently executing Phase 1 of a 7-phase GSD project plan: "Foundation — Docker Tooling, Simulador Host & NVM"

## Important Details
- **Machine**: Cricut Maker 1 Champagne with bootloader `cutcutgo-bl` already installed, connected via USB
- **MCU**: PIC32MX470F512L (512KB flash, 128KB RAM, MIPS, no FPU — use fixed-point in PID)
- **Memory**: flash 130/512 KB (76% free), RAM 58/131 KB (48 KB are RX/TX serial buffers recoverable)
- **Build**: XC32 v4.35 + PIC32MX_DFP 1.5.259 via Docker (`cutcutgo-builder:latest`), compiles clean with `-Werror`

- **No FPU** on PIC32MX — any PID/control algorithms must use Q15/Q16 fixed-point
- **No endstops** — homing via motor stall detection (encoder watchdog)
- **No current feedback** — A4950 chopping is hardware-only (LSS pin not routed to MCU ADC); pressure estimation via encoder lag + PWM/speed proxy
- **I2C on head connector** (SDA=RA3, SCL=RA2 on J500) — tool EEPROM detection, currently unused
- **User directives**: (1) HAL layer rewrite with better algorithms, (2) all tooling via Docker, (3) robustness + reliability + calibration algorithm with minimum deviation

## Assistant (build · mimo-v2.5-free · 11.9s)

_Thinking:_

The user is asking what was taking up the extra 600KB in the UF2 file. Let me explain concisely.

The old UF2 was 917,504 bytes (896 KB). The new one is 286,720 bytes (280 KB). The difference is 630,784 bytes (616 KB).

The old UF2 was built from a bin that was truncated to exactly 458,752 bytes (0x70000) — the full app region size as defined by the bootloader's flash layout. But the actual code only extends to 0x9D0321F8 (offset 0x221F8 from base 0x9D010000 = ~139 KB). So the extra was just zeros padding out the rest of the 448 KB app region that the code never touched.


The old truncation was hardcoded to the full app region size, while the new approach computes the actual code span dynamically, eliminating all those unused zero-padded bytes.

El binario anterior se truncaba a **exactamente 458 KB** (`truncate -s 458752`) porque cubría todo el rango de app que el bootloader define (0x1D010000–0x1D080000), aunque el código real solo llega a **offset 0x221F8** (~139 KB).

Los ~600 KB de más eran **ceros sin usar**: páginas de flash que el código nunca toca pero que el UF2 incluía igual. El UF2 nuevo calcula el span real desde `xc32-objdump -h` (las secciones `.reset`, `.vector_*`, `.app_excpt`, etc.) y trunca ahí.

```
Old: 458 KB (rango completo del bootloader) → 896 KB UF2
New: 140 KB (span real del código)          → 280 KB UF2
Δ:   ~318 KB de ceros eliminados            → ~616 KB UF2 menos
```

## Assistant (build · mimo-v2.5-free · 6.9s)

_Thinking:_

The user is asking if it's normal that the machine turned off after copying the UF2. This is normal behavior for UF2 bootloaders - when the UF2 file is copied to the virtual mass-storage drive, the bootloader processes the file, writes it to flash, and then resets the MCU. After the reset, the mass-storage drive disconnects and the new firmware boots.

This is the expected behavior: copy UF2 → bootloader writes to flash → MCU resets → mass-storage disappears → machine boots with new firmware.

Let me confirm this is normal and tell the user what to expect next.

Sí, es el comportamiento normal del bootloader UF2:

1. Copia el UF2 → la MSC virtual lo procesa
2. El bootloader escribe el código en flash
3. Se desconecta la unidad → **la máquina se resetea automáticamente**
4. Arranca con el firmware nuevo

Es el equivalente a "eject" del USB — el bootloader ya no expone la unidad porque terminó la escritura. Ahora la máquina debería estar arrancando con el firmware nuevo.

## Assistant (build · mimo-v2.5-free · 18.6s)

_Thinking:_

`BOOTLOADER_MODE` IS defined for the _bl build (`-DBOOTLOADER_MODE`). This means the `#ifndef BOOTLOADER_MODE` block in initialization.c is SKIPPED for the _bl build. The config pragmas (FNOSC, POSCMOD, FWDTEN, etc.) are NOT compiled for the bootloader build.But the config sections ARE in the ELF (at the correct addresses). This means the config values come from somewhere else — maybe the bootloader's own initialization code, or from a default value.Wait, the bootloader's own config is in the cutcutgo-bl project, not in our app. The app's config sections are being placed by our linker, but the values are defaults because the `#pragma config` directives are skipped.
 
So when `BOOTLOADER_MODE` is defined, the config pragma block gets skipped entirely, leaving the compiler to use default values for those config sections. The problem is that the linker is still placing these default config values into the output, which overwrites whatever the bootloader had set. The real issue is that the bootloader's config words live in its own flash and don't get touched by the UF2 flashing process, so the app's config sections are pointless—they're just overwriting values that should stay as-is. The solution is to discard these config sections entirely from the app build rather than placing them in memory.

**`-DBOOTLOADER_MODE` está definido para el build `_bl`** → los `#pragma config` se saltan → las secciones `.config_BFC02FFx` contienen valores por defecto del compiler (POSCMOD=3, FWDTEN=1). El linker los coloca en el flash y **sobreescribe las config words correctas** que ya estaban en la máquina.

Solución: descartar las secciones de config en el build `_bl` — el bootloader ya puso las config words correctas y el UF2 no las toca.

### Key Debugging Discoveries (from this session)
- **ROOT CAUSE of firmware crash identified and fixed**: Bootloader linker script `p32MX470F512H.bl.ld` was missing `/DISCARD/` for `.config_BFC02FFx` sections. `BOOTLOADER_MODE` define skips `#pragma config` directives in `initialization.c:58`, so sections contained compiler defaults (POSCMOD=OFF, FWDTEN=ON). The linker placed these, overwriting correct fuse values → MCU fell back to FRC 8 MHz → all clocks wrong → instant crash. **Fix: commit `147ae92`**
- **UF2 size issue identified and fixed**: Original UF2 (896KB) covered full app region (0x70000) but code only uses ~140KB. Bootloader MSC virtual drive only 438KB. **Fix: `tools/uf2_slim.py` computes real code span dynamically, commit `1b5edee` — UF2 now 280KB**
- **`DRV_FAT32_AsyncWrite` vs `DRV_FAT32_AsyncEraseWrite`**: Bootloader's FAT32 virtual driver only processes UF2 blocks via `AsyncEraseWrite` (mapped in `usb_device_init_data.c:115`). `AsyncWrite` (line 517) discards non-UF2 data silently. The `AsyncEraseWrite` path reads full 4KB page from flash, merges UF2 data, erases page, rewrites 8 rows. Config words at 0x1FC02FFx are OUTSIDE range check (`targetAddr >= 0x1D010000 && targetAddr < 0x1D080000`) → bootloader silently skips them.
- **Linux unmount of bootloader MSC hangs**: Virtual FAT32 driver doesn't properly respond to kernel unmount/flush syscalls. Workaround needed: force unmount (`timeout 5 fusermount -u`) or write directly to block device
- **Config words in HEX from `#pragma config` in `initialization.c:60-81`**: FNOSC=PRIPLL, POSCMOD=HS, FWDTEN=OFF, WDTPS=PS1048576 — correct when placed by standalone linker, but lost in _bl build
- **Original `eeprom.c` was a stub**: `eeprom_get_char` returned 0, `eeprom_put_char` did nothing (all AVR code under `#if 0`). Settings never persisted.
- **Picocom installed** via `pkexec pacman -S --noconfirm picocom` on host (CachyOS/Arch)
- **pyserial available** on host (`import serial` works)
- **Backup created**: `backups/phase01-20260831-090004/` — both ELFs, hexes, UF2, MD5SUMS, GIT-COMMIT.txt (gitignored)

    addr = 0x9D010000 + off
    b = bytes([data.get(addr+i, 0xFF) for i in range(4)])

# Decode first instruction as MIPS

if opcode == 0x03:

    target = (0x9D000000) | (target26 << 2)
    print(f'  -> JAL 0x{target:08X}')
elif opcode == 0x02:
    target26 = w0 & 0x3FFFFFF
    target = (0x9D000000) | (target26 << 2)
    print(f'  -> J 0x{target:08X}')
else:

### Key Debugging Discoveries (from this session)
- **Config-words fix did NOT solve the crash**: Commit `147ae92` added `/DISCARD/` for `.config_BFC02FFx` in `_bl` linker, HEX has 0 config records, but firmware still doesn't boot after UF2 flash
- **UF2 processing succeeds (MSD disappears)**: Bootloader processes the UF2 and resets, confirming UF2 data reaches the MCU. But after reset, app doesn't enumerate as USB serial — MSD reappears (04d8:0009 "Simple MSD Device Demo"), suggesting bootloader stays in bootloader mode or app crashes immediately
- **HEX file uses physical addresses (0x1D0xxxxx), not KSEG0 (0x9D0xxxxx)**: Initial Python scripts misparsed addresses; corrected parsing confirms reset vector at physical 0x1D010000 contains valid data (first instruction = JAL)
- **`udisksctl` works for unmount**: `udisksctl mount -b /dev/sde1` and `udisksctl unmount -b /dev/sde1` succeed without hanging (unlike raw `mount`/`umount` which hangs on the bootloader's virtual FAT32)
- **Bootloader `launch_app()`**: Reads first word at `APP_ADDR` (0x9D010000); if 0xFFFFFFFF stays in bootloader; otherwise calls `SYS_DeInitialize(NULL)`, disables interrupts, jumps via function pointer
- **`nvm_init()` called from `settings_init()` → `GRBL_Init()` → `APP_Initialize()` → `SYS_Initialize()`**: Flash wait states (`CHECON`) configured before `APP_Initialize()` — NVM flash reads should be safe
- **Original BL linker had NO config sections** and `LENGTH = 0x6E000`; our modified has `LENGTH = 0x6D000` (4KB shrink for NVM page) — code is 132KB, well within limit
- **Original `eeprom.c` was all `#if 0` stubs** — `eeprom_get_char` returned 0, `eeprom_put_char` did nothing. Settings never persisted.
- **`clk/plib_clk.c`**: `CLK_Initialize()` waits `while(!OSCCONbits.SLOCK)` — if PLL doesn't lock, hangs forever (no USB enumeration = crash symptom matches)

### Investigation Status
- **All NVM symbols link correctly** in the BL ELF (`nvm_init` @ `9d026820`, `nvm_read_byte` @ `9d02ee18`, etc.)
- **Code size is fine**: text=132KB, data=724B, bss=61KB — fits in 0x6D000 (446KB) program memory
- **Unconfirmed hypothesis**: Something in our changes causes a hang/crash during `SYS_Initialize()` → `APP_Initialize()` → `GRBL_Init()` before USB CDC enumerates. Most likely suspects in priority order:

  3. `nvm_init()` causing unexpected behavior when reading blank/invalid NVM page
  4. Build system not compiling NVM files correctly (unconfirmed — symbols exist in ELF)
- **Next diagnostic step**: Build a minimal firmware (strip NVM changes, keep only linker config discard) to isolate whether the crash is from NVM code or linker changes

## Objective
- Evolving cutcutgo firmware (GRBL 1.1 port for Cricut Maker 1 Champagne, PIC32MX470F512L) toward a reliable, self-calibrating CNC machine with robust homing, stall detection, tool detection, pressure estimation, and minimal deviation calibration
- Currently executing Phase 1 of a 7-phase GSD project plan: "Foundation — Docker Tooling, Simulador Host & NVM"
- **Immediate**: Firmware crash-on-boot investigation — stock v1.0 firmware ALSO fails to boot, proving the issue is NOT in our code changes. Root cause is toolchain (XC32 v4.35) or bootloader-related.

## Important Details
- **Machine**: Cricut Maker 1 Champagne with bootloader `cutcutgo-bl` already installed, connected via USB
- **MCU**: PIC32MX470F512L (512KB flash, 128KB RAM, MIPS, no FPU)
- **Memory**: flash 130/512 KB (76% free), RAM 58/131 KB (48 KB RX/TX serial buffers recoverable)
- **Build**: XC32 v4.35 + PIC32MX_DFP 1.5.259 via Docker (`cutcutgo-builder:latest`), compiles clean with `-Werror`
- **Bootloader NOT being modified** — only studied for NVM flash-write sequence and UF2 processing
- **NVM layout frozen**: `single-page-end` at `0x9D07F000` (user-approved one-way decision)
- **No FPU** — PID/control must use Q15/Q16 fixed-point
- **No endstops** — homing via motor stall detection (encoder watchdog)
- **No current feedback** — A4950 chopping hardware-only
- **I2C on head connector** (SDA=RA3, SCL=RA2 on J500) — tool EEPROM detection, unused
- **User directives**: (1) HAL layer rewrite with better algorithms, (2) all tooling via Docker, (3) robustness + reliability + calibration algorithm with minimum deviation
- **User language**: Spanish; technical terms/code stay English
- **searxng preferred** over webfetch for searches

### Critical Finding: Stock v1.0 firmware ALSO fails
- Built firmware from upstream tag `v1.0` in git worktree (`/tmp/stock-v1.0/`) using same Docker toolchain
- Same symptoms: MSD disappears (UF2 processed), then device vanishes from USB entirely (no MSD, no serial)
- Stock v1.0 linker has `/* /DISCARD/ : { *(.config_BFC02FFC) } */` **commented out** — config sections present in ELF
- Stock v1.0 ELF has `.config_BFC02FF0`–`.config_BFC02FFC` sections (4 bytes each at 0xBFC02FF0–0xBFC02FFC)
- `uf2_slim.py` truncates binary to app region span only, so config sections should NOT be in UF2 — yet stock still fails
- **Conclusion: problem is NOT our code changes. It's XC32 v4.35 toolchain producing incompatible binaries, or a bootloader issue.**

### Key Debugging Discoveries
- **Config-words fix did NOT solve the crash**: Commit `147ae92` added `/DISCARD/` for `.config_BFC02FFx` in `_bl` linker — firmware still doesn't boot
- **Proof-of-life test FAILED**: Added raw GPIO toggle (TRISET/LATE RE4) at very start of `main()` before `SYS_Initialize()` — app never reached `main()`. Confirms crash is BEFORE our NVM/init code
- **UF2 processing succeeds (MSD disappears)**: Bootloader processes UF2 and resets
- **Bootloader `launch_app()`**: Reads first word at `APP_ADDR` (0x9D010000); if 0xFFFFFFFF stays in bootloader; otherwise `SYS_DeInitialize(NULL)`, disables interrupts, jumps via function pointer
- **`udisksctl` works for mount/unmount**: `udisksctl mount -b /dev/sde1` / `udisksctl unmount -b /dev/sde1` succeed
- **`clk/plib_clk.c`**: `CLK_Initialize()` waits `while(!OSCCONbits.SLOCK)` — PLL hang possible
- **main() confirmed at `0x9d026af8`** (moved after proof-of-life code), entry `0x9d010000` → `_startup` at `0x9d010008` → crt0 → `_main_entry` at `0x9d02fd30` → `main()` → `SYS_Initialize()` → `SYS_Tasks()` loop

## Important Details
- **Machine**: Cricut Maker 1 Champagne with bootloader `cutcutgo-bl` already installed, connected via USB
- **MCU**: PIC32MX470F512L (512KB flash, 128KB RAM, MIPS, no FPU)
- **Memory**: flash 130/512 KB (76% free), RAM 58/131 KB (48 KB RX/TX serial buffers recoverable)
- **Build**: XC32 v4.35 + PIC32MX_DFP 1.5.259 via Docker (`cutcutgo-builder:latest`), compiles clean with `-Werror`
- **Bootloader NOT being modified** — only studied for NVM flash-write sequence and UF2 processing
- **NVM layout frozen**: `single-page-end` at `0x9D07F000` (user-approved one-way decision)
- **No FPU** — PID/control must use Q15/Q16 fixed-point
- **No endstops** — homing via motor stall detection (encoder watchdog)
- **No current feedback** — A4950 chopping hardware-only
- **I2C on head connector** (SDA=RA3, SCL=RA2 on J500) — tool EEPROM detection, unused
- **User directives**: (1) HAL layer rewrite with better algorithms, (2) all tooling via Docker, (3) robustness + reliability + calibration algorithm with minimum deviation
- **User language**: Spanish; technical terms/code stay English
- **searxng preferred** over webfetch for searches
- **Build workflow**: Sources must be physically copied (not symlinked) to `src/` at repo root for `find src -name '*.c'` to work in Docker. Build with: `docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/workspace -w /workspace cutcutgo-builder:latest bash -c "export PATH=/opt/microchip/xc32/v4.35/bin:\$PATH; make -f tools/Makefile.firmware CONF=cutcutgo_bl build-one TOLERANT=1"`

### Critical Finding: Problem is CODE, not toolchain
- **Stock v1.0 firmware compiled with XC32 v4.35 WORKS** — flashes and runs on machine ("el software arranco y se mueve")
- **Fork modified code compiled with same XC32 v4.35 CRASHES** — blue LED lights briefly then turns off, no USB serial
- User confirmed: "osea que el problema no es el toolkit, es el codigo"
- XC32 v4.20 download fails (403 Forbidden from Microchip) — not needed since v4.35 works for stock
- Bootloader source at `/tmp/opencode/cutcutgo-bl/`: `launch_app()` checks first word at 0x9D010000, calls `SYS_DeInitialize(NULL)`, disables interrupts, jumps to app
- HEX file uses Extended Linear Address records (type 04) — physical addresses 0x1D010000+
- UF2 pipeline verified: BIN→UF2 via `uf2_slim.py` → 286,720 bytes (560 blocks × 512), code span 143,360 bytes, 4KB-page aligned

### Bootloader Details (verified from source)
- `launch_app()`: reads `*(uint32_t*)(APP_ADDR)` → if 0xFFFFFFFF stays in bootloader, else `SYS_DeInitialize(NULL)`, `__builtin_disable_interrupts()`, `fptr()` jump to 0x9D010000
- `IsUsbMsdTriggered()`: checks first word + PAUSE button press
- Flash write: reads 4KB page, modifies 256 bytes, erases page, writes 8×512-byte rows
- UF2 safety: only writes blocks where `targetAddr ∈ [0x1D010000, 0x1D080000)`
- Config-words fix (commit `147ae92`): `/DISCARD/` all `.config_BFC02FFx` in `_bl` linker — prevents POSCMOD=HS/HSWR override

### CRASH-ON-BOOT: RESOLVED
- **Root cause**: Fork linker script (`p32MX470F512H.bl.ld`) had `/DISCARD/` for `.config_BFC02FF0/4/8/C` sections
- The compiler emits default config-word sections even when `BOOTLOADER_MODE` skips `#pragma config`
- The `/DISCARD/` removed these from the firmware binary; the bootloader's UF2 processing overwrote existing config registers with erased values (0xFFFFFFFF), breaking oscillator configuration
- **Fix**: Removed the `/DISCARD/` block; kept NVM page reserve + ASSERT
- **Evidence table**:
  - Stock v1.0 + original LD → ✓ WORKS
  - Fork code + original LD → ✓ WORKS (homing + USB)
  - Fork code + fork LD (with /DISCARD/) → ✗ CRASH
  - Fork code + fork LD (without /DISCARD/) → ✓ WORKS
- Commits: `e6cf2cc` (linker fix + proof-of-life), `ebcd234` (flash/test scripts), `922ab6f` (debug docs update)

- Currently executing Phase 1 of a 7-phase GSD project plan: "Foundation — Docker Tooling, Simulador Host & NVM"

## Important Details
- **Machine**: Cricut Maker 1 Champagne with bootloader `cutcutgo-bl` already installed, connected via USB
- **MCU**: PIC32MX470F512L (512KB flash, 128KB RAM, MIPS, no FPU)
- **Memory**: flash 130/512 KB (76% free), RAM 58/131 KB (48 KB RX/TX serial buffers recoverable)
- **Build**: XC32 v4.35 + PIC32MX_DFP 1.5.259 via Docker (`cutcutgo-builder:latest`), compiles clean with `-Werror`

- **NVM layout frozen**: `single-page-end` at `0x9D07F000` (user-approved one-way decision)
- **No FPU** — PID/control must use Q15/Q16 fixed-point
- **No endstops** — homing via motor stall detection (encoder watchdog)
- **No current feedback** — A4950 chopping hardware-only

- **User directives**: (1) HAL layer rewrite with better algorithms, (2) all tooling via Docker, (3) robustness + reliability + calibration algorithm with minimum deviation, (4) binary naming convention: always include task reference, save in build/dist/bin, never generic names like `test_N.uf2`

- **USB bus-powered**: `/dev/ttyACM0` exists even when machine is OFF (PIC32 powered by USB 5V). Only firmware response to `?` confirms MCU is running

## Objective
- Evolving cutcutgo firmware (GRBL 1.1 port for Cricut Maker 1 Champagne, PIC32MX470F512L) toward a reliable, self-calibrating CNC machine with robust homing, stall detection, tool detection, pressure estimation, and minimal deviation calibration
- Currently executing Phase 1 of a 7-phase GSD project plan: "Foundation — Docker Tooling, Simulador Host & NVM"
- **Immediate**: Recover machine from broken flash, then complete NVM physical tests with correct LED behavior

## Important Details
- **Machine**: Cricut Maker 1 Champagne with bootloader `cutcutgo-bl` already installed, connected via USB
- **MCU**: PIC32MX470F512L (512KB flash, 128KB RAM, MIPS, no FPU)
- **Memory**: flash 130/512 KB (76% free), RAM 58/131 KB (48 KB RX/TX serial buffers recoverable)
- **Build**: XC32 v4.35 + PIC32MX_DFP 1.5.259 via Docker (`cutcutgo-builder:latest`), compiles clean with `-Werror`
- **Bootloader NOT being modified** — only studied for NVM flash-write sequence and UF2 processing
- **NVM layout frozen**: `single-page-end` at `0x9D07F000` (user-approved one-way decision)
- **No FPU** — PID/control must use Q15/Q16 fixed-point
- **No endstops** — homing via motor stall detection (encoder watchdog)
- **No current feedback** — A4950 chopping hardware-only
- **I2C on head connector** (SDA=RA3, SCL=RA2 on J500) — tool EEPROM detection, unused
- **User directives**: (1) HAL layer rewrite with better algorithms, (2) all tooling via Docker, (3) robustness + reliability + calibration algorithm with minimum deviation, (4) binary naming convention: always include task reference, save in build/dist/bin, never generic names like `test_N.uf2`
- **User language**: Spanish; technical terms/code stay English
- **searxng preferred** over webfetch for searches
- **Build workflow**: Sources must be physically copied (not symlinked) to `src/` at repo root for `find src -name '*.c'` in Makefile. Build with Docker: `docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/workspace -w /workspace/cutcutgo.X cutcutgo-builder:latest make -f ../tools/Makefile.firmware CONF=cutcutgo_bl all TOLERANT=1`
- **Python testing**: virtualenv at `.venv/` with pyserial; any Python deps go there
- **uf2_slim.py requires**: objdump, ELF, bin, uf2conv.py, output UF2, base address — invoked from Makefile `uf2` target from `cutcutgo.X/` working directory
- **Docker build permissions**: Docker runs as root; fix ownership with `docker run --rm ... chown -R 1000:1000` after build

### Critical Hardware Behaviors Discovered
- **USB bus-powered**: `/dev/ttyACM0` exists even when machine is OFF (PIC32 powered by USB 5V). Only firmware response to `?` confirms MCU is running
- **Machine turns OFF after UF2 flash** — does not reboot; user must physically press power button
- **After UF2 flash + power-on, USB port may change** (e.g. `/dev/ttyACM0` → `/dev/ttyACM1`)
- **During boot, machine does homing (carriage moves right)**, LED should blink during this but currently doesn't — user wants this fixed
- **White LED = normal operation**, blue LED = only during proof-of-life/boot
- **PIC32 USB CDC blocks `serial.write()`** due to `tcdrain()` — must use `os.write()` to bypass
- **`dsrdtr=False` required** to prevent PIC32 reset on serial port open
- **pyserial `reset_input_buffer()` only clears host-side receive buffer**, NOT firmware-side input buffer — stale data from previous commands causes `STATUS_INVALID_STATEMENT` errors. Fix: send `\r\n` first to flush firmware buffer

### HAL LED System
- **6 LEDs**: `LED_LOGO` (RB11), `LED_PAUSE` (RB10), `LED_UPDOWN` (RF13), `LED_POWER_WHITE` (RF4), `LED_POWER_RED` (RF5), `LED_POWER_BLUE` (RE4)
- **HAL API**: `led_set()`, `led_clear()`, `led_toggle()`, `led_blink_mode()`, `led_normal_mode()`, `led_set_power(blue, white, red)`
- **`led_handle_blink()`** called from `timer.c` — toggles LEDs in `LED_BLINK` mode every `LED_BLINK_PERIOD` (250ms)
- **`led_init()`** called from `app.c` during `SYS_Initialize()`
- **`grbl.h` includes `hal/led.h`** — LED API available in GRBL source files
- **User directive**: LED should be **off only when powered** (rail control), **steady on when idle**, **blinking during homing/setup operations** — `LED_OFF()` should NOT be used in normal operation
- **`st_go_idle()` should only LED_ON if `sys.state == STATE_IDLE`** (avoids LED during alarm/init before serial ready)

### MSD Mount: udisksctl (no root needed)
- User added to `disk` group (`pkexec usermod -aG disk r2d2`)
- `udisksctl mount -b /dev/sdd1` mounts at `/run/media/r2d2/Cutcutgo`

### CRASH-ON-BOOT: RESOLVED
- **Root cause**: Fork linker script (`p32MX470F512H.bl.ld`) had `/DISCARD/` for `.config_BFC02FF0/4/8/C` sections
- Fix: Removed the `/DISCARD/` block; kept NVM page reserve + ASSERT
- Commits: `e6cf2cc` (linker fix + proof-of-life), `ebcd234` (flash/test scripts), `922ab6f` (debug docs update)

### NVM test `send()` `error:3` mystery: RESOLVED
- **Root cause**: pyserial `reset_input_buffer()` only clears host RX buffer, not firmware input buffer. Stale data from previous commands concatenated with `$110=500` → firmware parsed invalid parameter → `STATUS_INVALID_STATEMENT` (error:3)
- **Fix**: `send()` now flushes firmware input buffer by sending `\r\n` first, consuming response, then sending actual command
- `MAX_STEP_RATE_HZ` is commented out (`config.h:314`), so step rate check is NOT active — not the cause
